# Skip when the edge already counted the click

> The redirect handler skips recording a click if the `x-edge-click-recorded` header is `1`, preventing double-counting when the edge worker already recorded it.

_Part of [Recording a click without slowing the redirect](fire-and-forget-click-recording.md)_

Short links are cached at Cloudflare's edge for speed, so a popular link's request might be served from cache without hitting the origin. The edge can record the click there. When the origin does handle a request, it needs to know whether the edge already recorded it, to avoid counting the same click twice. The `redirect` handler checks the `x-edge-click-recorded` header: if it's `1`, the edge recorded it already, so the origin skips calling `recordClick`. Otherwise, the origin records via [Recording a click without slowing the redirect](fire-and-forget-click-recording.md), which sends the click event without blocking the redirect.

**Look at:** [`redirect` in share-links.controller.ts](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/marketing/api/share-links.controller.ts#L40)

## Watch out

- The header value must be exactly the string `'1'`—other values or a missing header won't trigger the skip, so the edge must set it with exact coordination
- Click metadata like country and referer come only from whichever side (edge or origin) actually records it; if the edge records most clicks, origin-recorded clicks won't have edge-provided geolocation
- If the edge stops recording or the header fails to propagate, the origin will start recording clicks that the edge already counted, creating temporary duplicates until downstream deduplication catches them
